messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Spike in 5xx and connection resets observed for ingress-euc2 (particularly euc2c) beginning 2026-03-10T09:40Z. Autopager sent to #incidents and on-call.
sam (oncall): ack. I'm standing up the triage channel. grabbing dashboards and runbook.
tia-netops: seeing repeated TCP RSTs between NLB and envoy targets, plus incrementing nf_conntrack_count on node pool euc2c. flow logs show lots of half-open connections from a subset of client IPs.
pablo-sre: 5xx breakdown: 502 from envoy upstream reset, 504 from backend timeouts. p95 latency high for /v1/generate. envoy logs show keepalive timeouts and "connection reset by peer" on upstream.
jen-support: Customer reports: "charts-host" and "Streamly" reported tokenization errors and retries at ~09:41Z. Support has opened tickets and notified AMs.
sam (oncall): quick plan: 1) validate conntrack exhaustion on nodes 2) apply temporary conntrack increase on euc2c 3) rotate ingress pods on euc2c one-by-one 4) reduce NLB idle timeout and upstream keepalive to break long-lived half-closed sockets 5) if errors persist, shift traffic weight to euc3. tia, can you check NLB target health config?
tia-netops: checking target groups. I see target deregistration delay is default 300s; targets flapping while draining may keep sockets around. Suggest lowering deregistration delay to 60s for ingress target group during mitigation.
pablo-sre: running conntrack check: ssh node ip-10-3-12-77: /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count=245000, nf_conntrack_max=262144 -> nearing limit but not exceeded. however kernel timers show many TIME_WAIT sockets. seems client behavior creates many short-lived connections.
sam (oncall): running one-off sysctl to raise nf_conntrack_max to 500k on euc2c nodes. using daemonset job: ```kubectl -n kube-system run conntrack-bump --image=alpine --restart=OnFailure -- /bin/sh -c "for f in $(kubectl get nodes -l zone=euc2c -o name); do kubectl debug $f --image=alpine -- sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=500000; done"```
deploy-bot: Job conntrack-bump created.
tia-netops: applied NLB changes: set target-group deregistration_delay=60 and NLB idle-timeout=60s for ingress targets. also added lifecycle hook to drain connections gracefully.
pablo-sre: rolling restart ingress-controller pods on euc2c one-at-a-time to clear conntrack entries: ```kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/ingress-controller --selector topology.kubernetes.io/zone=euc2c --max-unavailable=1```
deploy-bot: Rolling restart started. pod ingress-ctrl-8cdf restarted, passed readiness.
jen-support: customers report partial recovery at 09:46Z, some still seeing errors. continuing to log incidents.
sam (oncall): after conntrack bump and restarts, RSTs have decreased ~60% in the last 3m. 5xx rate reduced but p95 still elevated. planning gradual DNS weight shift to euc3: move 30% traffic for 15m to validate. TTL is 20s. executing Route53 change now.```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z9ABC --change-batch file://shift-30-to-euc3.json```
deploy-bot: Route53 change submitted (change id C-89432). expect ~20-40s propagation.
tia-netops: after weight shift, error rate fell to near baseline for majority of traffic; remaining errors concentrated on long-lived websocket connections used by a small set of clients. those clients continue to hold half-closed sockets causing conntrack churn.
pablo-sre: creating follow-up tasks: 1) long-term: tune kernel TIME_WAIT and conntrack garbage collection, 2) evaluate enabling TCP_REPAIR and reuse settings, 3) add alert when nf_conntrack_count > 70% of max, 4) review client SDKs that maintain aggressive reconnects.
enforcement-bot: Note: changed deregistration_delay for target-group tg-ingress-euc2 to 60s (temporary).
sam (oncall): status update: mitigations applied: nf_conntrack increased, ingress pods rotated, NLB idle/deregistration lowered, partial DNS failover to euc3. Customer impact window: 09:40Z-09:48Z (majority of errors between 09:41-09:46Z). Monitoring for 45m before closing.
jen-support: compiled customer impact summary and shared with PM/CS. will open a dedicated customer comms thread.
pablo-sre: postmortem owner assigned: @pablo-sre. action items created in backlog (IDS-4578). will include recommended runbook updates and an investigation into client connection patterns.
sam (oncall): thanks all for fast responses. leaving incident in monitoring state; paging escalation clear. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident recorded as SEV2. Auto-handoff: Observability lead to follow-up for 24h monitoring.
